### Observed differences

- Three activities dropped out of the flow. In the earlier window A19 ran in about 36 of 100 traces, A20 in about 31 and A25 in about 35; in the later window A19 and A25 appear in none of the 200 traces, and A20 in only 1. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- In the earlier window these three were mutually exclusive alternatives — a trace contained one of them or none, essentially never two — while in the later window virtually no trace contains any of them. [REL007, REL009, REL014]
- The routing into this group changed at A41. Earlier, A41's observed outgoing transitions split roughly evenly between A19 (about 33 in 100), A25 (about 33) and A20 (about 27); in the later window about 92 in 100 go directly to A26. [DIR004]
- Earlier, each of the three led almost exclusively to A26 (about 97–99 of 100 of their observed outgoing transitions). In the later window A19 and A25 show no observed outgoing transitions, and the single trace containing A20 continues to A30 instead. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- Co-occurrence of the three activities with their partners collapsed: with A14, A26 and A41 from roughly 31–36 of 100 traces to zero (A20: one trace), and with A12 and A24 from roughly 10–17 of 100 to about zero. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL008, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]
- A41 and A26 became adjacent: earlier the pair was typically two event positions apart (about 94 of 100 observed pairs), in the later window typically one step apart (about 93 of 100). [LAG002]
- Smaller shifts: A24–A31 pairs are now usually one step apart (about 59 of 100, up from about 39); A26 sits slightly earlier within traces while A14 and A41 sit slightly later; A12 appears in somewhat more traces (about 42 of 100 before, about 51 after). [LAG001, POS005, POS001, POS006, REL001, REL002, REL003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the alternative branch formed by A19, A20 and A25 between A41 and A26 is no longer executed in the later window: A41, which previously handed over to exactly one of the three in roughly equal shares, now leads directly to A26, and the three activities themselves are almost entirely unobserved. The change is shown directly and consistently across indicator families — the participation collapse, the redirection of A41's outgoing transitions, the loss of every co-occurrence with partner activities, and the A41–A26 distance shrinking from typically two steps to one, which fits a bypass rather than a mere re-weighting of the old paths. The volume of qualifying control-flow items (36 against fewer than 1 expected for an unchanged process) also makes a chance explanation of the ensemble implausible. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR004, DIR001, DIR003, LAG002, REL004, REL010, REL019]

Limitations: zero participation strictly means only that the activities were not observed, so the evidence cannot distinguish a removed branch from one that still exists but is chosen in almost no case; and the single later trace in which A20 continues to A30 instead of A26 rests on one observation and could reflect a residual rerouted path. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR002]

Other differences: A24–A31 pairs occur one step apart more often than before, A14, A26 and A41 show small positional shifts within traces, and A12 appears in somewhat more traces; these are not part of the main hypothesis. [LAG001, POS001, POS005, POS006, REL001, REL002, REL003]
